title: fastpatch-watchlist-notes-gabrielle-2028-05-09
content:
Shift: 2028-05-09 AM (04:45-13:00)
Owner: Gabrielle Moreno (half-watch)
Context: quiet night until a mid-morning spike in host p95 for serving-runtime in us-west-2. Two pages escalated: P1 latency increase + noisy kv-cache miss alerts.

TIMELINE
- 06:10 — quick health alerts for batcher-queue-length (short bursts). Ignored (brief).
- 09:12 — Pager: SRE-3421 (latency spike). Initial Slack thread: #oncall -> @gabrielle.
- 09:14 — Opened trace link (observability): heavy tail on decode kernel on a couple of pods (serve-runtime-v2).
- 09:17 — SSH jump to host-rt-09; noticed high iowait on ephemeral EBS (unrelated?)
- 09:20 — Noticed steady kv-cache miss-rate ~ 7% over 5m. Alert fired: kv-cache-miss >5% (5m).
- 09:30 — Canary fallback to smaller model variant triggered for some routes; traffic routing kicked in (console shows automatic fallback).
- 09:42 — Mitigation: temporarily bumped batcher max_batch_events from 64 -> 96 for the affected pool (fast path) to smooth latency.
- 10:05 — Latency p95 returned near baseline; kv-cache miss-rate back to ~2.5%.
- 11:00 — Deployed a small config change (PR#2567) to reduce aggressive cache eviction (staged).

INCIDENT NOTES
- Root cause hypothesis: transient cache churn due to a spike of novel prefix patterns from a customer load test (unannounced). KV cache was thrashing because prefix cardinality spiked; combined with slightly underprovisioned host IO for a subset of pods caused decode kernel slowdowns.
- Why fallback triggered: smart routing saw degraded latency on serve-runtime-v2 pool and routed to cheaper-but-smaller variants. This prevented 100% user-facing errors but increased token-cost due to more shorter-model fallbacks.
- Impact: ~3 minutes of elevated p95 for ~300 requests/s for a small customer segment; no user-facing errors; cost delta ~+$0.6 for the window.

ACTIONS TAKEN (what I did)
- Pulled traces and flamegraphs, pasted to thread (obs link).
- Increased batcher max_batch_events temporarily (rollback note below).
- Toggled a canary route to pinned model for a handful of test routes to validate behavior.
- Opened JIRA SRE-3421 and linked PR#2567 for the cache tuning change.

FOLLOW-UPS / TODOs (assignments)
- [ ] Runbook update: add a section for "kv-cache thundering / prefix-cardinality" including mitigation steps (owner: Mira Chen)
- [ ] Add an alert refinement: kv-cache-miss > 5% should require correlating with prefix-cardinality metric before paging (owner: me / Gabrielle)
- [ ] Retro blurb for oncall rotation: request product to warn SREs before large-scale load tests (owner: Ravi)
- [ ] Investigate host-rt-09 iowait spikes -> possible EBS noisy neighbor (owner: infra team, ticket INF-881)
- [ ] Add a synthetic to reproduce prefix-cardinality spike in staging and measure cache eviction churn (owner: eng-serving-runtime, label: perf-test)
- [ ] Rollback note: revert batcher max_batch_events to 64 once stable window confirmed (owner: me)

RUNBOOK TODO (quick bullets to add into confluence runbook)
- Detection: combine kv-cache-miss-rate + prefix-cardinality (new metric) + decode-kernel-latency heatmap.
- Immediate mitigations: 1) increase batcher max_batch_events (quick), 2) pin heavy routes to smaller-model fallback manually, 3) spin up additional pool capacity (autoscale policy temporary increase).
- Longer term: smarter eviction policy (LRU + frequency), TTL tuning per-model, and prefix-aware caching heuristics.

QUICK COMMANDS / PLAYBOOK STEPS I RAN
- kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=serve-runtime -o wide
- ssh ops@host-rt-09 (checked dmesg, iostat)
- curl -s "https://console.redwood-internal/obs/query?trace=SRE-3421" (pasted link into thread)
- redis-cli --bigkeys (spot-checked key distribution on kv-cache-proxy staging)

NOTES FOR NEXT SHIFT
- If kv-cache-miss spikes again, first check prefix-cardinality dashboard before paging whole SRE team.
- Confirm PR#2567 rollout plan: staged canary -> full rollout only after 24h of stability.
- Follow up with product on unannounced customer load test (who, when, expected qps).

OPEN QUESTIONS
- Was the load test internal (eng) or external customer? Slack thread unsure. Who ran it?
- Can autoscaler warm additional pool faster for this workload class? Current warm-up is ~2m; need to evaluate.

RANDOM SCRATCH (notes to self)
- Idea: add a tiny server-side sampler that captures prefix histogram for high-variance routes (cheap; sampled 0.1%) to drive eviction heuristics.
- Check PR#2412 notes — had earlier attempt at prefix-aware cache but NACKed for complexity. Maybe revisit with simpler heuristic.

END OF SHIFT
- Left notes in ticket SRE-3421, will follow up with Mira on runbook update.
- Rollback batcher to 64 at 12:30 after stability window.

Quick sign-off: gabrielle
